records.literal_gloss: In the month the eighth, in year two of Darius, came [the] word of Yahweh to Zechariah son of Berechiah son of Iddo the prophet, saying:

en.L: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying:
en.B: In the eighth month of the second year of Darius's reign, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah the prophet, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo:
en.R: In the eighth month of the year, in Darius's second year as king, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave a message to the prophet Zechariah. Zechariah was the son of Berechiah and the grandson of Iddo. This is the message:

fr.L: Le huitième mois, la deuxième année de Darius, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée à Zacharie fils de Bérékia, fils d’Iddo, le prophète, disant :
fr.B: Le huitième mois de la deuxième année du règne de Darius, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée au prophète Zacharie, fils de Bérékia, fils d’Iddo :
fr.R: Le huitième mois de l’année, la deuxième année où Darius était roi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné un message au prophète Zacharie. Zacharie était le fils de Bérékia et le petit-fils d’Iddo. Voici ce message :

es.L: En el mes octavo, en el año segundo de Darío, vino la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} a Zacarías hijo de Berequías, hijo de Ido, el profeta, diciendo:
es.B: En el mes octavo del segundo año del reinado de Darío, la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino al profeta Zacarías hijo de Berequías, hijo de Ido:
es.R: En el octavo mes del año, en el segundo año de Darío como rey, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio un mensaje al profeta Zacarías. Zacarías era hijo de Berequías y nieto de Ido. Este es el mensaje:

sw.L: Katika mwezi wa nane, katika mwaka wa pili wa Dario, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilimjia Zekaria mwana wa Berekia, mwana wa Ido, nabii, kusema:
sw.B: Katika mwezi wa nane wa mwaka wa pili wa utawala wa Dario, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilimjia nabii Zekaria mwana wa Berekia, mwana wa Ido:
sw.R: Katika mwezi wa nane wa mwaka, katika mwaka wa pili wa Dario kuwa mfalme, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimpa nabii Zekaria ujumbe. Zekaria alikuwa mwana wa Berekia na mjukuu wa Ido. Huu ndio ujumbe:

vi.L: Tháng thứ tám, năm thứ hai đời Đa-ri-út, lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với Xa-cha-ri con trai Bê-rê-kia, con trai Y-đô, nhà tiên tri, rằng:
vi.B: Tháng tám, năm thứ hai triều Đa-ri-út, lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với nhà tiên tri Xa-cha-ri con trai Bê-rê-kia, cháu Y-đô:
vi.R: Vào tháng tám, năm thứ hai Đa-ri-út làm vua, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban một sứ điệp cho nhà tiên tri Xa-cha-ri. Xa-cha-ri là con trai Bê-rê-kia và cháu Y-đô. Đây là sứ điệp ấy:

ko.L: 다리오 제2년 여덟째 달에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 잇도의 손자 베레갸의 아들 예언자 스가랴에게 임하여 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: 다리오가 다스린 지 2년째 되는 해 여덟째 달에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 잇도의 손자 베레갸의 아들 예언자 스가랴에게 임했다.
ko.R: 다리오가 왕이 된 지 2년째 되는 해 여덟째 달에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 예언자 스가랴에게 말씀을 주셨다. 스가랴는 베레갸의 아들이고 잇도의 손자였다. 그 말씀은 이러하다.

pt.L: No oitavo mês, no segundo ano de Dario, a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a Zacarias, filho de Berequias, filho de Ido, o profeta, dizendo:
pt.B: No oitavo mês, no segundo ano de Dario, a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio ao profeta Zacarias, filho de Berequias, filho de Ido:
pt.R: No oitavo mês do ano, no segundo ano em que Dario era rei, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} deu uma mensagem ao profeta Zacarias. Zacarias era filho de Berequias e neto de Ido. Esta é a mensagem:

decisions.choice: the eighth month of the second year of Darius: October to November 520 BC
decisions.reason: Darius I was king of Persia from 522 to 486 BC, and Judah was a small province of his empire. The months are counted from the spring, so the eighth month fell in the autumn; it began late in October 520 BC. No day is given. Zechariah's first message came two months after Haggai's first (Haggai 1:1, the sixth month of the same year), in the weeks between Haggai's messages of the seventh and the ninth months (Haggai 2:1, 10). The work on the temple had begun again about two months before (Haggai 1:14-15). The modern date is worked out from the Babylonian calendar, which the Jews used after the exile.

decisions.choice: Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo: a prophet among the exiles who came back from Babylon
decisions.reason: Ezra names Haggai and Zechariah as the two prophets who urged the people to rebuild the temple (Ezra 5:1; 6:14). There Zechariah is called "son of Iddo", using "son" for a descendant, as Hebrew often does; here his father Berechiah is named as well. Nehemiah 12:4 and 16 list Iddo as the head of a priestly family that returned with Zerubbabel, and a Zechariah as its head in the next generation, so the prophet was most likely a priest as well. His name means "the LORD remembers".

decisions.choice: the prophet: Zechariah's title
decisions.reason: The title stands at the end of the line of names, so it could go with Iddo, the last name. But the book is about Zechariah's prophecy, the same heading returns in verse 7, and Ezra 5:1 calls Zechariah a prophet.

decisions.choice: Zechariah son of Berechiah in Matthew 23:35
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the blood of "Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar" (Matthew 23:35). The killing of a Zechariah in the temple court is told of Zechariah son of Jehoiada in 2 Chronicles 24:20-22. Readers have explained Matthew's wording in more than one way. This book says nothing about how the prophet Zechariah died.

decisions.choice: in the second year of Darius (L); of Darius's reign (B); in Darius's second year as king (R); the word of the LORD came to (L, B); gave a message to (R)
decisions.reason: The date keeps the Hebrew form, as set for Haggai and Zechariah: "the second year of Darius's reign" at Balanced and "Darius's second year as king" at Readable, as in Jeremiah's dated headings. Readable says "of the year" for the month but does not change the date into the modern calendar; the decision above gives it. The heading formula follows the table for "the word of the LORD came to". Readable puts the names in a sentence of their own and says "grandson", since Iddo was Berechiah's father.

decisions.choice: Dated headings and narrative in the passé simple at L and B and the passé composé at R; the LORD's words are speech; the messages Zechariah is told to deliver take no quotation marks
alternatives: quotation marks around "Ainsi parle …" in 1:3, as the English
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for the Twelve: the prophet's own message ("dis-leur : Ainsi parle …") is unquoted, while words quoted inside it (the former prophets in 1:4, the fathers in 1:6) take « ».

decisions.choice: "Zacharie fils de Bérékia, fils d'Iddo"; dates as Haggai ("la deuxième année de Darius" L, "du règne de Darius" B, "où Darius était roi" R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's names; the dated headings follow Haggai 1:1.

decisions.choice: "Zacarías hijo de Berequías, hijo de Ido"
decisions.reason: The published forms of Chronicles and Ezra; Matthew 23:35 in Spanish has "Baraquías", from the Greek, but the Old Testament form is kept here. The date follows the Hebrew form at each level, as in Haggai.

decisions.choice: "Zekaria mwana wa Berekia, mwana wa Ido"
decisions.reason: The prophet keeps the Old Testament form "Zekaria", as Ezra 5:1. Matthew 23:35 names "Zakaria mwana wa Barakia" in the New Testament form; the two spellings are kept apart, and the English allusion decision gives the link. The dated heading follows Haggai 1:1.

decisions.choice: "잇도의 손자 베레갸의 아들 예언자 스가랴" at every level
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms. Ezra 5:1 names him by his grandfather; Matthew 23:35 in Korean has "바라갸의 아들 사가랴", the Greek spelling, which the meaning decision discusses. The date follows the Kings formula, as Haggai.

decisions.choice: "Xa-cha-ri con trai Bê-rê-kia", with "cháu Y-đô" (B, R) and "con trai Y-đô" (L)
decisions.reason: The terms note's names (Bê-rê-kia as 1 Chronicles 6:24; Y-đô as 2 Chronicles 9:29). Matthew 23:35 has "Ba-ra-chi", the Greek form of Berechiah; the allusion decision names it.

decisions.choice: dated headings as in Haggai: Hebrew order at Literal, "năm thứ hai triều Đa-ri-út" (B), "năm thứ hai Đa-ri-út làm vua" (R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide for Zechariah: the dated headings take the terms note's form. Through the night visions of chapters 1-6, "the angel who talked with me" is "thiên sứ đang nói với tôi" at every level, and where the Hebrew has only "he" the narrative calls him "người", lowercase, with no span; the angel says "tôi" and "ông", and Zechariah says "thưa chúa tôi" (L, B) / "thưa ngài" (R); "I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look" is "tôi ngước mắt lên và thấy, kìa" (L) / "tôi ngước mắt nhìn lên và thấy" (B) / "tôi nhìn lên và thấy" (R); the horses' colours are set at 1:8. The night visions are prose with straight double quotes.

decisions.choice: no Nº mês, no Nº ano de Dario (L, B); no Nº ano em que Dario era rei (R); a palavra do SENHOR veio a (L, B); deu uma mensagem a (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (1:7; 7:1): the dated headings keep one wording at each level, with ordinal numbers in words and the formula Haggai 1:1 and 2:10 have in Portuguese for the same king's years ("no segundo ano de Dario" at Literal and Balanced, "no segundo ano em que Dario era rei" at Readable), as the English keeps one wording for Haggai and Zechariah (r-en-1). "A palavra do SENHOR veio a" is the formula Hosea 1:1 and Jeremiah 1:2 set; Readable has the LORD give a message, as the English Readable does. The king is "Dario", as Ezra 4-6 has him in Portuguese.

decisions.choice: Zacarias, filho de Berequias, filho de Ido
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the prophet is "Zacarias", the usual Brazilian form, and his grandfather "Ido", as Ezra 5:1 and 6:14 name them in Portuguese; "Berequias" is the usual Brazilian form of his father's name (m2). "Filho de" stands between commas, as Isaiah 1:1 and Jeremiah 1:1 name their prophets; Readable says "neto" for Iddo, as the English Readable says "grandson".

records.literal_gloss: Was angry Yahweh with your fathers [with] anger.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with your fathers with [great] anger.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was very angry with your ancestors.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was very angry with your ancestors.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} {{deity_pronoun:s’|S’}}est irrité contre vos pères d’une [grande] colère.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a été très en colère contre vos ancêtres.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a été très en colère contre vos ancêtres.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se enojó con {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}} con [gran] enojo.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se enojó mucho con {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se enojó mucho con {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giận tổ phụ các ngươi bằng [cơn] giận [lớn].
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã rất giận tổ tiên các ngươi.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã rất giận tổ tiên các ngươi.

pt.L: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} se irou contra os pais de vocês com [grande] ira.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} ficou muito irado com os antepassados de vocês.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} ficou com muita raiva dos antepassados de vocês.

decisions.choice: angry with anger: very angry
decisions.reason: The verb is followed by its own noun, "was angry ... anger", a Hebrew way of making a statement strong. The anger is past: it fell on the generations before the exile, and verse 15 calls it a little anger compared with the anger the LORD now feels toward the nations.

decisions.choice: your fathers: your ancestors, the generations before the exile
decisions.reason: "Fathers" is used for forebears in general. The ancestors of Zechariah's hearers were the people of Judah whose sins brought the fall of Jerusalem and the exile (2 Kings 24:3-4; 2 Chronicles 36:15-16). "Your" is plural: the people of Zechariah's own day are addressed.

decisions.choice: fathers (L); ancestors (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Jeremiah, Literal keeps "fathers" and the other levels say "ancestors", which is what the word means here and includes mothers as well. Literal shows the strengthening with the bracketed "great"; the other levels say "very angry".

decisions.choice: "padres" (L); "antepasados" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The fathers are the earlier generations; B and R say "antepasados", as the English says "ancestors", with plural_you on the possessive.

decisions.choice: "babu zenu" (B, R); "baba zenu" (L)
decisions.reason: The fathers are the generations before the exile; "babu" (forebears) says so at B and R, as the English "ancestors".

decisions.choice: os pais de vocês (L); os antepassados de vocês (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): Literal keeps "pais", Balanced and Readable say "antepassados" (m2). "De vocês" makes plain that the hearers are addressed, where "seus" could mean "their"; the same words return in verses 4-6.

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֗ם כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת שׁ֣וּבוּ אֵלַ֔י נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְאָשׁ֣וּב אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will say to them, Thus says Yahweh of hosts: Return to me, declaration of Yahweh of hosts, and I will return to you, says Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: So say to them, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, that I may return to you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts."
en.B: So tell them, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, and I will return to you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies."
en.R: So tell the people, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, and I will come back to you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies."

fr.L: Tu leur diras donc : Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Revenez à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, et je reviendrai à vous, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: Dis-leur donc : {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : Revenez à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, et je reviendrai à vous, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: Dis donc au peuple : Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Revenez à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, et je reviendrai vers vous, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.

es.L: Y les dirás: «Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: {{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, y yo me volveré a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos».
es.B: Así que diles: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: {{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, y yo me volveré a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos».
es.R: Así que dile al pueblo: «Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: {{plural_you:Regresen|Volved}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, y yo regresaré a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos».

sw.L: Basi uwaambie, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Nirudieni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawarudia ninyi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi."
sw.B: Basi waambie, "Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Nirudieni, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawarudia, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi."
sw.R: Basi waambie watu, "Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Nirudieni, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawarudia, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi."

vi.L: Vậy hãy nói với họ: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán thế này: Hãy trở lại cùng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán vậy, thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trở lại cùng các ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán."
vi.B: Vậy hãy nói với họ: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán như vầy: Hãy trở lại cùng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán vậy, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trở lại cùng các ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán."
vi.R: Vậy hãy nói với dân chúng: "Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán: Hãy trở về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trở lại với các ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán."

ko.L: 그러므로 너는 그들에게 말하여라. "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 나에게 돌아오너라. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. 그러면 나도 너희에게 돌아가겠다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다."
ko.B: 그러므로 너는 그들에게 전하여라. "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 나에게 돌아오너라. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 그러면 나도 너희에게 돌아가겠다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다."
ko.R: 그러므로 너는 백성에게 전하여라. "하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 나에게 돌아오너라. 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 그러면 나도 너희에게 돌아가겠다. 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다."

pt.L: Portanto, dize-lhes: "Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos: Voltem para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, e eu voltarei para vocês, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos."

decisions.choice: return to me, and I will return to you: the people's turning and God's turning toward them in favor
decisions.reason: The same verb is used both ways. For the people it means turning away from their evil ways back to the LORD (verse 4); for the LORD it means turning back to them with favor after the years of anger. Malachi 3:7 repeats the call almost word for word, and verse 16 says that the LORD has returned to Jerusalem. The order of the sentence calls the people to turn, and promises that God will meet them.

decisions.choice: say to them: a command to the prophet about the people of his day
decisions.reason: The verb form is the one Hebrew uses to carry on a command, so "you will say" means "say". "Them" are the people of Zechariah's day, whose ancestors were named in verse 2.

decisions.choice: three formulas in one verse: the message is the LORD's own word
decisions.reason: The verse names the LORD of hosts three times, with "thus says", "declares" and "says". The Hebrew uses two different words: the first and last are the ordinary verb "says"; the middle one is the noun used for a solemn declaration. Piling them up stresses that the call to return comes from the LORD himself. On the title "the LORD of hosts", which runs through Zechariah, see the note at Isaiah 1:9.

decisions.choice: Thus says ... declares ... says the LORD of hosts (L); The LORD of Armies says this ... declares ... says (B); This is what the LORD of Armies says ... says ... says (R)
decisions.reason: The formulas follow the wording set for the prophets: "declares the LORD" for the solemn declaration, "says the LORD" for the plain verb, and "the LORD of hosts" at Literal and "the LORD of Armies" at the other levels. Readable says "says" for both, as the table sets, and "come back" for "return". Literal says "that I may return", since the Hebrew joins the promise to the call with a simple "and" that can express purpose. The words Zechariah is to speak stand in double quotation marks.

decisions.choice: *shuv* "revenir" at every level, both for the people and for the LORD
decisions.reason: As the French prophets: "revenir" keeps the play between the people's return and God's.

decisions.choice: "Así dice ... declara ... dice" (L); "dice esto ... afirma ... dice" (B); "dice" (R)
decisions.reason: Zechariah's formulas follow the Spanish prophets at each level; the LORD of hosts is "de los ejércitos" at L and "de los Ejércitos" at B and R. Shuv is "volverse" for repentance, as the term sheet sets.

decisions.choice: "CHÚA Vạn Quân phán vậy" for ne'um and "CHÚA Vạn Quân phán" for 'amar (L, B); "phán" for both at R
decisions.reason: The terms note keeps "phán vậy" at Literal and Balanced for ne'um, so the three formulas of this verse stay distinct.

decisions.choice: "trở lại cùng Ta" (L, B) / "trở về với Ta" (R) for shuv
decisions.reason: The Jeremiah note: repentance is "quay về, trở lại cùng Ta"; the same verb is used for God's turning back so the play of the verse is kept.

decisions.choice: *shuv* is "돌아오다" for the people and "돌아가다" for God ("나도 너희에게 돌아가겠다") at every level
decisions.reason: As Jeremiah, *shuv* is "돌아오다", and "회개하다" stays for the Greek; Korean marks the direction of each turning, so God's answering turn is "돌아가다", which keeps the same verb root.

decisions.choice: "Nirudieni" ... "nitawarudia" at every level
decisions.reason: The verb shuv is "kurudi" for both the people's turning and God's, as the Jeremiah block sets, so the two halves of the promise mirror each other in Swahili too.

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives that mean God, mid-sentence ("nami", "naye", "mimi", "kwangu", "wangu", "yake"), never on verb prefixes
alternatives: a span on every pronoun, as in English
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for God inside the verb ("Nirudieni", "nitawarudia"), and a verb prefix or object marker cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun span stands only on free pronouns and possessives. Zechariah therefore has fewer spans in Swahili than in English. Mid-sentence, every free pronoun or possessive that means God takes the span, including "mimi", "nami", "naye", "yeye" and "kwangu", even where the English has none; a word that opens a sentence is written plainly with its capital, and "naye" followed by a noun ("naye BWANA") is a conjunction with no span. This holds for the whole book, as in Ezekiel and the rest of the Twelve.

decisions.choice: Assim diz ... declara ... diz o SENHOR dos Exércitos (L, B); É isto que o SENHOR dos Exércitos diz ... diz ... diz (R)
alternatives: o SENHOR dos Exércitos (L), o SENHOR Todo-Poderoso (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the formulas keep the words Isaiah 1:9, 1:24 and 7:7 set in Portuguese for the prophets: "Assim diz" (L, B) and "É isto que ... diz" (R) for the messenger formula, "declara" (L, B) and "diz" (R) for ne'um. The title is "o SENHOR dos Exércitos" at every level, as Isaiah has it, where the English Balanced and Readable say "of Armies": Portuguese "Exércitos" already says armies, so one wording serves all three levels.

decisions.choice: Voltem para mim ... e eu voltarei para vocês (every level); dize-lhes (God to Zechariah)
alternatives: Convertam-se a mim ... e eu me converterei a vocês
decisions.reason: The same verb both ways (m1), so Portuguese uses "voltar" both ways at every level; Malachi 3:7 has the same call in Portuguese, "Voltem para mim, e eu voltarei para vocês", at every level, as Joel 2:12 has "voltem para mim", and these words match it. God speaks to Zechariah with "tu" ("dize-lhes"; Readable "diz ao povo"), as he speaks to Ezekiel (Ezekiel 3:11), and to the people with "vocês".

records.literal_gloss: Do not be like your fathers, to whom called the prophets the former, saying, Thus says Yahweh of hosts: Turn back now from your ways evil and your deeds evil; and not they listened and not they paid attention to me, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: Do not be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets called out, saying, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Turn back, please, from your evil ways and your evil deeds." But they did not listen, and they did not pay attention to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Do not be like your ancestors, to whom the earlier prophets called out, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Turn back from your evil ways and your evil deeds." But they would not listen or pay attention to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Do not be like your ancestors. Long ago the prophets called out to them, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Turn away from the evil way you live and the evil things you do." But your ancestors would not listen. They paid no attention to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

Ils n’ont pas fait attention à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

ko.R: 너희는 너희 조상들처럼 되지 마라. 오래전에 예언자들이 그들에게 외쳤다. "하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 너희의 악한 생활과 악한 행동에서 돌아서라." 그러나 너희 조상들은 듣지 않았다. 그들은 나에게 귀를 기울이지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

pt.L: Não sejam como os pais de vocês, a quem os profetas antigos clamaram, dizendo: "Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos: Voltem, por favor, dos seus maus caminhos e das suas más obras." Mas eles não quiseram ouvir nem dar atenção a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

Muito tempo atrás, os profetas clamaram a eles: "É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos diz: Abandonem o jeito mau como vocês vivem e as coisas más que vocês fazem." Mas os antepassados de vocês não quiseram ouvir. Não deram atenção a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: the former prophets: the prophets before the exile, and their call to turn back
decisions.reason: The earlier prophets are those who spoke before Jerusalem fell. Their call is summed up in words very close to Jeremiah's: "Turn now, each of you, from his evil way and your evil deeds" (Jeremiah 25:5; compare 18:11; 35:15), and 2 Kings 17:13 sums up the message of all the prophets the same way. Zechariah sets his message in line with theirs.

decisions.choice: please: a small word that softens a command into an appeal
decisions.reason: The word is often left untranslated. Here it makes "turn back" a plea as well as an order: the prophets begged the people to turn.

decisions.choice: and your deeds: the form the Hebrew text tells the reader to read
decisions.reason: The written letters of the Hebrew text and the form marked to be read aloud differ slightly in spelling here. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: they did not listen ... did not pay attention: the ancestors refused the call
decisions.reason: The two verbs are a pair that Jeremiah often uses for Judah's refusal (Jeremiah 6:10; 7:24, 26). The LORD speaks of himself as "me": the prophets' words were his words.

decisions.choice: please (L); not shown (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable let the tone of the sentence carry the plea; an added "please" would sound weak in a command from God. Readable says "the evil way you live" for "your evil ways", and names the ancestors again for clarity.

decisions.choice: Voltem, por favor (L); Deixem (B); Abandonem (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the softening word (m2) as "por favor" and the verb "voltar" of verse 3. Balanced and Readable let the plea sound in the command, as the English does (r-en-1), and use a verb of leaving the evil ways, the plain Portuguese for turning away from them.

decisions.choice: two questions that need no answer: both generations have died
alternatives: the people's reply, that the prophets are dead too
decisions.reason: The ancestors are gone, carried off by the judgment the prophets warned of. The prophets were mortal as well. The point comes in verse 6: people die, but the LORD's words did not die with them; they caught up with the ancestors. A few readers take the second question as the hearers' answer back to the prophet ("and the prophets, are they still alive?"), but nothing marks a change of speaker.

decisions.choice: Where are your ancestors now? And did the prophets live forever?
decisions.reason: Readable puts the questions in ordinary order. Its second question looks back to the earlier prophets, which is what the Hebrew means.

source.text: אַ֣ךְ׀דְּבָרַ֣י וְחֻקַּ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוִּ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־עֲבָדַ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים הֲל֥וֹא הִשִּׂ֖יגוּ אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וַיָּשׁ֣וּבוּ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר זָמַ֜ם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָ֔נוּ כִּדְרָכֵ֨ינוּ֙ וּכְמַ֣עֲלָלֵ֔ינוּ כֵּ֖ן עָשָׂ֥ה אִתָּֽנוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: But my words and my statutes which I commanded my servants the prophets, did not they overtake your fathers? And they repented and said, Just as planned Yahweh of hosts to do to us, according to our ways and according to our deeds, so he has done with us.

en.L: Yet {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes that I commanded {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets, have they not overtaken your fathers? Then they turned back and said, "Just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts purposed to deal with us, according to our ways and according to our deeds, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has dealt with us."
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} decrees, the ones I commanded {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets to speak, did they not catch up with your ancestors? Then they repented and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has dealt with us as our ways and our deeds deserved, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} planned to do."
en.R: But the words and the laws that I gave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets to speak, did they not catch up with your ancestors? Then they turned back and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has done to us what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} planned to do. He has punished us for the way we lived and for the things we did."

fr.L: Pourtant {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} prescriptions que j’avais ordonnées à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} serviteurs les prophètes, n’ont-elles pas atteint vos pères ? Alors ils sont revenus et ont dit : « Comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées avait projeté d’agir envers nous, selon nos chemins et selon nos actions, ainsi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a agi envers nous. »
fr.B: Mais {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} décrets, ceux que j’avais ordonné à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} serviteurs les prophètes d’annoncer, n’ont-ils pas rattrapé vos ancêtres ? Alors ils se sont repentis et ont dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées nous a traités comme nos chemins et nos actions le méritaient, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’avait décidé. »
fr.R: Mais les paroles et les lois que j’ai données à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} serviteurs les prophètes pour qu’ils les annoncent, n’ont-elles pas rattrapé vos ancêtres ? Alors ils sont revenus à Dieu et ont dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées nous a fait ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait décidé de faire. Il nous a punis pour la manière dont nous avons vécu et pour ce que nous avons fait. »

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} estatutos que mandé a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} siervos los profetas, ¿no alcanzaron a {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}}? Entonces se volvieron y dijeron: «Tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos se propuso hacer con nosotros, conforme a nuestros caminos y conforme a nuestras obras, así {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha hecho con nosotros».
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} decretos, los que mandé anunciar a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} siervos los profetas, ¿no alcanzaron a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}? Entonces se arrepintieron y dijeron: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos nos ha tratado como merecían nuestros caminos y nuestras obras, tal como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se lo había propuesto».
es.R: Pero las palabras y las leyes que di a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} siervos los profetas para que las anunciaran, ¿no alcanzaron a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}? Entonces se volvieron a Dios y dijeron: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos nos ha hecho lo que se había propuesto. Nos ha castigado por la manera en que vivíamos y por lo que hacíamos».

sw.L: Lakini maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kanuni {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} nilizowaamuru watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} manabii, je, hazikuwapata baba zenu? Ndipo wakarudi, wakasema, "Kama vile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi alivyokusudia kututendea, sawasawa na njia zetu na sawasawa na matendo yetu, ndivyo alivyotutendea."
sw.B: Lakini maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kanuni {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, zile nilizowaamuru watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} manabii wazitangaze, je, hazikuwafikia babu zenu? Ndipo walipotubu na kusema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi ametutendea kama njia zetu na matendo yetu yalivyostahili, kama alivyokusudia kufanya."
sw.R: Lakini maneno na sheria nilizowapa watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} manabii ili wazitangaze, je, hazikuwafikia babu zenu? Ndipo wakarudi, wakasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi ametutendea kile alichokusudia kufanya. Ametuadhibu kwa sababu ya jinsi tulivyoishi na mambo tuliyoyatenda."

vi.L: Thế nhưng lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và luật lệ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền cho các đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là các tiên tri, chẳng phải đã đuổi kịp tổ phụ các ngươi sao? Bấy giờ họ quay lại và nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã định xử với chúng ta thể nào, theo đường lối chúng ta và theo việc làm chúng ta, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã xử với chúng ta thể ấy."
vi.B: Nhưng lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và các luật lệ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, những điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền cho các đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là các tiên tri rao báo, chẳng phải đã theo kịp tổ tiên các ngươi sao? Bấy giờ họ ăn năn và nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã xử với chúng ta đúng như đường lối và việc làm của chúng ta đáng phải chịu, y như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã định."
vi.R: Nhưng những lời và luật lệ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ban cho các đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là các tiên tri để rao báo, chẳng phải đã theo kịp tổ tiên các ngươi sao? Bấy giờ họ ăn năn quay về và nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã làm cho chúng ta đúng như điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã định. Ngài đã phạt chúng ta vì lối sống và những việc chúng ta đã làm."

ko.L: 그러나 내가 나의 종 예언자들에게 명령한 나의 말과 나의 규례가 너희 조상들을 따라잡지 않았느냐? 그러자 그들이 돌이켜 말했다. "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리의 길과 우리의 행위대로 우리에게 하시려고 작정하신 그대로 그분께서 우리에게 하셨다."
ko.B: 그러나 내가 내 종 예언자들에게 전하라고 명령한 내 말과 내 규례가 결국 너희 조상들을 따라잡지 않았느냐? 그러자 그들이 회개하며 말했다. "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 계획하신 그대로 우리의 길과 행위에 맞게 우리에게 하셨다."
ko.R: 그러나 내가 내 종 예언자들에게 전하게 한 말과 법이 너희 조상들을 따라잡지 않았느냐? 그러자 그들이 돌이켜 말했다. "하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 계획하신 대로 우리에게 하셨다. 그분께서는 우리가 살아온 대로, 우리가 한 일대로 우리를 벌하셨다."

pt.L: Mas as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras e os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} estatutos, que ordenei aos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} servos, os profetas, não alcançaram os pais de vocês? Então eles se voltaram e disseram: "Assim como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos planejou fazer conosco, segundo os nossos caminhos e segundo as nossas obras, assim {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fez conosco."
pt.B: Mas as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras e os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} decretos, que ordenei aos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} servos, os profetas, que anunciassem, não alcançaram os antepassados de vocês? Então eles se arrependeram e disseram: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos nos tratou como mereciam os nossos caminhos e as nossas ações, exatamente como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha planejado fazer."
pt.R: Mas as palavras e as leis que eu dei aos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} servos, os profetas, para anunciarem, não alcançaram os antepassados de vocês? Então eles se arrependeram e disseram: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos fez conosco o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha planejado fazer. Ele nos castigou pelo jeito como vivemos e pelas coisas que fizemos."

decisions.choice: overtake: catch up with someone, as a pursuer does
decisions.reason: The verb is used in the covenant warnings: if the people do not obey, "all these curses will come on you and overtake you" (Deuteronomy 28:15, 45). The prophets died, but the words they spoke kept on running and caught the ancestors.

decisions.choice: they repented: the ancestors, when the judgment fell
alternatives: the people of Zechariah's day, who answered his call
decisions.reason: The nearest subject is "your fathers", and the sentence reads most naturally as their confession after the disaster came, like the prayers of the exiles (Lamentations 2:17; Daniel 9:11-14). It can also be read as a report of how Zechariah's own hearers responded to verses 3-5, as the people answered Haggai (Haggai 1:12). The verse does not settle it.

decisions.choice: just as the LORD purposed to do: the judgment was what God had planned and warned of
decisions.reason: Lamentations 2:17 makes the same confession with the same verb: "The LORD has done what he purposed; he has carried out his word." The disaster was not chance: God did what he said he would do, and he did it in keeping with what the people had done.

decisions.choice: statutes: the decrees God laid down
decisions.reason: The word means something fixed by decree. Joined with "words", it covers both the warnings and the laws the prophets were sent to press on the people.

decisions.choice: The LORD of Armies has dealt with us as our ways and our deeds deserved (B); He has punished us for the way we lived (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the main clause first, which English finds easier. Readable says "punished us", which is what "dealt with us according to our ways" means here, and "statutes" becomes "laws".

decisions.choice: "estatutos" (L), "decretos" (B), "leyes" (R)
decisions.reason: Huqqim follows the English levels' range; "siervos" is kept for the prophets at every level, as the Spanish prophets do.

decisions.choice: "kanuni" (L, B); "sheria" (R)
decisions.reason: Chuqqim as the Pentateuch's statutes ("kanuni" at L and B) and the Ezekiel table ("sheria" at R). "Watumishi wangu manabii": the prophets are "servants" at every level, with the span on God's possessive.

decisions.choice: "luật lệ" for chuqqim
decisions.reason: The terms note: statute is "luật lệ" at every level, as in the Pentateuch note.

decisions.choice: "they repented" (*shuv*) is "돌이켜" (L, R) and "회개하며" (B)
decisions.reason: Here *shuv* is a change of mind after judgment, not a return from exile; the English Balanced says "repented", which Korean says with "회개하다", while Literal and Readable keep the turning picture.

decisions.choice: *chuqqim* is "규례" (L, B) and "법" (R); "my servants the prophets" is "나의 종 예언자들" (L) and "내 종 예언자들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's words for *chuqqot* and for "servant".

decisions.choice: alcançaram (every level)
decisions.reason: "Alcançar" is the Portuguese verb for a pursuer catching up with someone, the picture of the covenant warnings (m1), and plain enough for Readable.

source.text: בְּיוֹם֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֜ה לְעַשְׁתֵּֽי־עָשָׂ֥ר חֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הוּא־חֹ֣דֶשׁ שְׁבָ֔ט בִּשְׁנַ֥ת שְׁתַּ֖יִם לְדָרְיָ֑וֶשׁ הָיָ֣ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־זְכַרְיָה֙ בֶּן־בֶּ֣רֶכְיָ֔הוּ בֶּן־עִדּ֥וֹא הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: On day twenty and four of the eleventh month, it [is the] month of Shebat, in year two of Darius, came [the] word of Yahweh to Zechariah son of Berechiah son of Iddo the prophet, saying:

en.L: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, that is, the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying:
en.B: On the twenty-fourth day of Shebat, the eleventh month, in the second year of Darius's reign, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah the prophet, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo:
en.R: On the twenty-fourth day of Shebat, the eleventh month of the year, in Darius's second year as king, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave another message to the prophet Zechariah, the son of Berechiah and grandson of Iddo. This is the message:

fr.L: Le vingt-quatrième jour du onzième mois, c’est-à-dire le mois de Shebat, la deuxième année de Darius, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée à Zacharie fils de Bérékia, fils d’Iddo, le prophète, disant :
fr.B: Le vingt-quatrième jour de Shebat, le onzième mois, la deuxième année du règne de Darius, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée au prophète Zacharie, fils de Bérékia, fils d’Iddo :
fr.R: Le vingt-quatrième jour de Shebat, le onzième mois de l’année, la deuxième année où Darius était roi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné un autre message au prophète Zacharie, fils de Bérékia et petit-fils d’Iddo. Voici ce message :

es.L: El día veinticuatro del mes undécimo, que es el mes de Sebat, en el año segundo de Darío, vino la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} a Zacarías hijo de Berequías, hijo de Ido, el profeta, diciendo:
es.B: El día veinticuatro de Sebat, el mes undécimo, en el segundo año del reinado de Darío, la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino al profeta Zacarías hijo de Berequías, hijo de Ido:
es.R: El día veinticuatro de Sebat, el undécimo mes del año, en el segundo año de Darío como rey, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio otro mensaje al profeta Zacarías, hijo de Berequías y nieto de Ido. Este es el mensaje:

sw.L: Siku ya ishirini na nne ya mwezi wa kumi na moja, yaani, mwezi wa Shebati, katika mwaka wa pili wa Dario, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilimjia Zekaria mwana wa Berekia, mwana wa Ido, nabii, kusema:
sw.B: Siku ya ishirini na nne ya Shebati, mwezi wa kumi na moja, katika mwaka wa pili wa utawala wa Dario, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilimjia nabii Zekaria mwana wa Berekia, mwana wa Ido:
sw.R: Siku ya ishirini na nne ya Shebati, mwezi wa kumi na moja wa mwaka, katika mwaka wa pili wa Dario kuwa mfalme, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimpa nabii Zekaria, mwana wa Berekia na mjukuu wa Ido, ujumbe mwingine. Huu ndio ujumbe:

vi.L: Ngày hai mươi bốn tháng thứ mười một, tức là tháng Sê-bát, năm thứ hai đời Đa-ri-út, lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với Xa-cha-ri con trai Bê-rê-kia, con trai Y-đô, nhà tiên tri, rằng:
vi.B: Ngày hai mươi bốn tháng Sê-bát, tức tháng mười một, năm thứ hai triều Đa-ri-út, lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với nhà tiên tri Xa-cha-ri con trai Bê-rê-kia, cháu Y-đô:
vi.R: Ngày hai mươi bốn tháng Sê-bát, tức tháng mười một, năm thứ hai Đa-ri-út làm vua, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban một sứ điệp khác cho nhà tiên tri Xa-cha-ri, con trai Bê-rê-kia và cháu Y-đô. Đây là sứ điệp ấy:

ko.L: 다리오 제2년 열한째 달, 곧 스밧 월 이십사일에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 잇도의 손자 베레갸의 아들 예언자 스가랴에게 임하여 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: 다리오가 다스린 지 2년째 되는 해 열한째 달인 스밧 월 이십사일에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 잇도의 손자 베레갸의 아들 예언자 스가랴에게 임했다.
ko.R: 다리오가 왕이 된 지 2년째 되는 해 열한째 달인 스밧 월 24일에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 잇도의 손자이자 베레갸의 아들인 예언자 스가랴에게 또 말씀을 주셨다. 그 말씀은 이러하다.

pt.L: No vigésimo quarto dia do décimo primeiro mês, que é o mês de Sebate, no segundo ano de Dario, a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a Zacarias, filho de Berequias, filho de Ido, o profeta, dizendo:
pt.B: No vigésimo quarto dia do décimo primeiro mês, o mês de Sebate, no segundo ano de Dario, a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio ao profeta Zacarias, filho de Berequias, filho de Ido:
pt.R: No dia vinte e quatro de Sebate, o décimo primeiro mês do ano, no segundo ano em que Dario era rei, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} deu outra mensagem ao profeta Zacarias, filho de Berequias e neto de Ido. Esta é a mensagem:

decisions.choice: the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, Shebat, in Darius's second year: February 519 BC
decisions.reason: This is about the middle of February 519 BC, three months after verse 1. It is exactly two months after the day on which Haggai gave his last two messages (Haggai 2:10, 20), and five months after work on the temple began again (Haggai 1:15). Shebat is the Babylonian name of the month, which the Jews took up during the exile; this is its only use in the Bible.

decisions.choice: one heading for a series of visions in one night
decisions.reason: The heading speaks of Zechariah by name, and the report that follows speaks in his own voice: "I saw in the night" (verse 8). This one heading covers the eight night visions of 1:8-6:8, and the book gives no new date until 7:1. The visions are told as seen in a single night, though the text does not say so in so many words.

decisions.choice: the dated heading as in verse 1
decisions.reason: The date and the heading follow the wording of verse 1 at each level. Readable puts the month's name first and adds "another", since this is the second message.

decisions.choice: Zechariah's night visions (1:8-6:8) told in the first person: "je vis", "il me dit" (L, B), "j'ai vu", "il m'a dit" (R); the dialogue in « » with “ ” inside, running across verses
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: first-person narrative follows the narrative tenses, as Ezekiel's visions and Revelation.

decisions.choice: "Sebat"
decisions.reason: The Babylonian month name, in the Spanish spelling that matches the published "Tebet" and "Quisleu".

decisions.choice: "Shebati"
decisions.reason: The month name is new in the published Swahili; it follows the usual pattern for Hebrew names (a final -i after a consonant).

decisions.choice: "tháng Sê-bát" for Shebat
decisions.reason: A new month name, transliterated in the Protestant manner; the culture decision gives the modern date.

decisions.choice: Shebat is "스밧 월"
decisions.reason: The month name in its Protestant spelling, after the Korean month number as the Hebrew gives both.

decisions.choice: o mês de Sebate; no dia vinte e quatro (R)
decisions.reason: The Babylonian month name (m1) is written as Portuguese writes its sounds, "Sebate", with a capital, as Esther and Nehemiah have "Nisã", "Adar" and "Tebete". Readable gives the day as Brazilians say dates, "no dia vinte e quatro"; Literal and Balanced keep the ordinal of verse 1's heading.

records.literal_gloss: I saw the night, and look, a man riding on a horse red, and he [was] standing among the myrtles which [were] in the hollow, and behind him horses red, sorrel, and white.

en.L: I saw in the night, and look, a man riding on a red horse! And he was standing among the myrtles that [were] in the hollow, and behind him [were] horses, red, sorrel and white.
en.B: I saw a vision in the night: there was a man mounted on a red horse. He stood among the myrtle trees in the ravine, and behind him were red, sorrel and white horses.
en.R: During the night I saw a vision. A man was riding a red horse. He was standing among the myrtle trees in a deep valley. Behind him were horses that were red, reddish brown and white.

fr.L: Je vis pendant la nuit, et voici, un homme monté sur un cheval roux ! Et il se tenait parmi les myrtes qui [étaient] dans le creux, et derrière lui [il y avait] des chevaux roux, alezans et blancs.
fr.B: J’eus une vision pendant la nuit : un homme était monté sur un cheval roux. Il se tenait parmi les myrtes, dans le ravin, et derrière lui il y avait des chevaux roux, alezans et blancs.
fr.R: Pendant la nuit, j’ai eu une vision. Un homme était monté sur un cheval roux. Il se tenait parmi les myrtes, dans une vallée profonde. Derrière lui, il y avait des chevaux roux, brun-rouge et blancs.

es.L: Vi de noche, y he aquí, un hombre montado sobre un caballo rojo. Y él estaba entre los mirtos que [había] en la hondonada, y detrás de él [había] caballos rojos, alazanes y blancos.
es.B: Tuve una visión de noche: había un hombre montado en un caballo rojo. Estaba entre los mirtos de la hondonada, y detrás de él había caballos rojos, alazanes y blancos.
es.R: Durante la noche tuve una visión. Vi a un hombre montado en un caballo rojo. Estaba entre los mirtos en un valle profundo. Detrás de él había caballos rojos, de color café rojizo y blancos.

sw.L: Niliona usiku, na tazama, mtu amepanda farasi mwekundu! Naye alikuwa amesimama kati ya mihadasi iliyokuwa [katika] bonde, na nyuma yake [walikuwa] farasi wekundu, wa rangi ya kahawia na weupe.
sw.B: Niliona maono usiku: palikuwa na mtu aliyepanda farasi mwekundu. Alisimama kati ya mihadasi bondeni, na nyuma yake kulikuwa na farasi wekundu, wa rangi ya kahawia na weupe.
sw.R: Usiku niliona maono. Mtu mmoja alikuwa amepanda farasi mwekundu. Alikuwa amesimama kati ya mihadasi katika bonde lenye kina. Nyuma yake kulikuwa na farasi wekundu, wa rangi ya kahawia nyekundu, na weupe.

vi.L: Ban đêm tôi thấy, và kìa, một người cưỡi một con ngựa hồng! Người đứng giữa những cây sim [ở] trong chỗ trũng, và phía sau người [có] những con ngựa hồng, ngựa nâu đỏ và ngựa bạch.
vi.B: Ban đêm tôi thấy một khải tượng: có một người cưỡi ngựa hồng. Người đứng giữa những cây sim trong khe núi, và phía sau người có những con ngựa hồng, ngựa nâu đỏ và ngựa bạch.
vi.R: Trong đêm ấy, tôi thấy một khải tượng. Một người đang cưỡi một con ngựa màu đỏ. Người đứng giữa những cây sim trong một thung lũng sâu. Phía sau người có những con ngựa màu đỏ, màu nâu đỏ và màu trắng.

ko.L: 내가 밤에 보았다. 보라, 한 사람이 붉은 말을 타고 있었다! 그는 골짜기에 있는 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있었고, 그 뒤에는 붉은 말들과 밤색 말들과 흰 말들이 [있었다].
ko.B: 내가 밤에 환상을 보았다. 한 사람이 붉은 말을 타고 있었다. 그는 골짜기에 있는 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있었고, 그 뒤에는 붉은 말과 밤색 말과 흰 말들이 있었다.
ko.R: 밤에 나는 환상을 보았다. 한 사람이 붉은 말을 타고 있었다. 그는 깊은 골짜기에 있는 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있었다. 그 뒤에는 붉은 말과 붉은 갈색 말과 흰 말들이 있었다.

pt.L: Eu vi de noite, e eis que um homem montado num cavalo vermelho! E ele estava parado entre as murtas que [estavam] na baixada, e atrás dele [havia] cavalos vermelhos, castanhos e brancos.
pt.B: Tive uma visão de noite: havia um homem montado num cavalo vermelho. Ele estava parado entre as murtas, no fundo do vale, e atrás dele havia cavalos vermelhos, castanhos e brancos.
pt.R: Durante a noite, tive uma visão. Um homem estava montado num cavalo vermelho. Ele estava parado entre as murtas, num vale fundo. Atrás dele havia cavalos vermelhos, marrom-avermelhados e brancos.

decisions.choice: the first of eight night visions: horses that patrol the earth
decisions.reason: Chapters 1-6 report eight visions (1:8-17; 2:1-4; 2:5-17; 3:1-10; 4:1-14; 5:1-4; 5:5-11; 6:1-8). In each, Zechariah sees a picture, asks what it means, and an angel explains it. In this first one, riders who have gone throughout the earth report that it is quiet, and the LORD answers with comfort for Jerusalem. The book keeps the pictures as they were seen and lets the angel's words explain them; it does not say what each color means.

decisions.choice: the man on the red horse: the angel of the LORD of verse 11
decisions.reason: The man is described as "standing among the myrtle trees" in verses 8 and 10, and in verse 11 the same words are used of the angel of the LORD. So the rider is an angel in human form, the leader of the horsemen. He is not the angel who explains the visions (verse 9).

decisions.choice: myrtle trees: evergreen shrubs that grow near water
decisions.reason: The myrtle has dark, fragrant leaves and grows in damp, low places. Isaiah names it among the trees God will make grow when he restores his people (Isaiah 41:19; 55:13), and the returned exiles used its branches for the booths at the Festival of Booths (Nehemiah 8:15).

decisions.choice: in the hollow: a low, shaded place, a ravine or deep valley
alternatives: in the deep (a picture of the depths of the sea)
decisions.reason: The word is related to words for the depths of the sea (Exodus 15:5; Jonah 2:4) and is used here for a low place where myrtles grow. Some read it as a hint of the deep waters, others as a ravine near Jerusalem. The Greek translation reads "between the mountains", perhaps under the influence of 6:1. The sense of the scene does not depend on it.

decisions.choice: sorrel: reddish brown
decisions.reason: The word is rare (Isaiah 16:8 uses a related word for choice vines) and seems to name a reddish or brownish color. The colors of the horses are not explained in this vision; the riders are simply scouts sent out by the LORD (verse 10). Compare the colored horses of 6:2-3, which are partly different.

decisions.choice: look (L); there was (B); not shown (R); a vision (B, R); ravine (B), deep valley (R); reddish brown (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "look", the word that marks something seen in a vision; Balanced says "there was", and Readable simply tells what he saw. Balanced and Readable add "a vision", which the whole passage makes plain. Readable says "reddish brown" for the rare color word.

decisions.choice: "he aquí" (L), "había" (B), "Vi" (R); "mirtos"; "alazanes" (L, B), "café rojizo" (R)
decisions.reason: Visions follow the term sheet: L "Vi ..., y he aquí", B "Tuve una visión ... había", R "Vi". Myrtle is "mirto", as Isaiah 41:19 and 55:13 in Spanish.

decisions.choice: "mihadasi" (myrtles), as Isaiah 55:13; "wa rangi ya kahawia" (sorrel)
decisions.reason: The myrtle is "mhadasi", the word the published Isaiah uses. Sorrel, a reddish-brown horse, has no single Swahili word, so it is described by its colour.

decisions.choice: myrtle is "화석류나무"; sorrel is "밤색" (L, B) and "붉은 갈색" (R)
decisions.reason: "화석류나무" is the established Korean Bible word for the myrtle (Isaiah 41:19; 55:13); the colours follow the English levels. Zechariah narrates in the first person in the plain style, and gives God -시-.

decisions.choice: "cây sim" for the myrtles
decisions.reason: As Isaiah 55:13 in Vietnamese. The man is "người", lowercase and with no deity span: the meaning decision makes him the angel of the LORD, who takes no span (terms note).

decisions.choice: horse colours "ngựa hồng", "ngựa nâu đỏ", "ngựa bạch" (L, B) / "ngựa màu đỏ", "màu nâu đỏ", "màu trắng" (R)
decisions.reason: One set of colour words for the horses of both visions (1:8; 6:2-6): the same Hebrew colour takes the same word, "ngựa hồng", "ngựa ô", "ngựa bạch" and "ngựa đốm" at Literal and Balanced, the plain colour words at Readable. Sorrel is "nâu đỏ", the reddish brown of the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: eis que (L); havia (B); not shown (R); as murtas; a baixada (L), o fundo do vale (B), um vale fundo (R); castanhos (L, B), marrom-avermelhados (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: hinneh in the visions is "eis que" at Literal, as in Ezekiel's visions, and Balanced and Readable tell what was seen (r-en-1). The myrtle (m3) is "murta", its everyday Brazilian name. The low place (m4) is "baixada" at Literal and a deep valley at Balanced and Readable. The rare colour word (m5) is "castanho", the Portuguese word for a reddish-brown horse; Readable spells it out.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֖ר מָה־אֵ֣לֶּה אֲדֹנִ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י הַמַּלְאָךְ֙ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֔י אֲנִ֥י אַרְאֶ֖ךָּ מָה־הֵ֥מָּה אֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said, What [are] these, my lord? And said to me the angel who talks with me, I will show you what these [are].

en.L: And I said, "What [are] these, my lord?" And the angel who talked with me said to me, "I myself will show you what these are."
en.B: I asked, "What are these, my lord?" The angel who talked with me answered, "I will show you what they are."
en.R: I asked, "What are these, my lord?" The angel who talked with me said, "I will show you what they are."

fr.L: Et je dis : « Que [sont] ceux-ci, mon seigneur ? » Et l’ange qui parlait avec moi me dit : « Moi, je te montrerai ce que sont ceux-ci. »
fr.B: Je demandai : « Que sont ces chevaux, mon seigneur ? » L’ange qui parlait avec moi répondit : « Je vais te montrer ce qu’ils sont. »
fr.R: J’ai demandé : « Que sont ces chevaux, mon seigneur ? » L’ange qui parlait avec moi m’a dit : « Je vais te montrer ce qu’ils sont. »

es.L: Y dije: «¿Qué [son] estos, mi señor?». Y el ángel que hablaba conmigo me dijo: «Yo te mostraré qué son estos».
es.B: Pregunté: «¿Qué son estos, mi señor?». El ángel que hablaba conmigo me respondió: «Yo te mostraré lo que son».
es.R: Pregunté: «¿Qué son estos, señor?». El ángel que hablaba conmigo me dijo: «Te mostraré lo que son».

sw.L: Nami nikasema, "Hawa [ni] nini, bwana wangu?" Na malaika aliyezungumza nami akaniambia, "Mimi mwenyewe nitakuonyesha hawa ni nini."
sw.B: Nikauliza, "Hawa ni nini, bwana wangu?" Malaika aliyezungumza nami akajibu, "Nitakuonyesha maana yake."
sw.R: Nikauliza, "Hawa ni nini, bwana wangu?" Malaika aliyezungumza nami akasema, "Nitakuonyesha maana yake."

vi.L: Tôi nói: "Thưa chúa tôi, những [vật] này là gì?" Thiên sứ đang nói với tôi bảo tôi: "Chính tôi sẽ cho ông thấy những vật này là gì."
vi.B: Tôi hỏi: "Thưa chúa tôi, những vật này là gì?" Thiên sứ đang nói với tôi đáp: "Tôi sẽ cho ông thấy chúng là gì."
vi.R: Tôi hỏi: "Thưa ngài, những vật này là gì?" Thiên sứ đang nói với tôi đáp: "Tôi sẽ cho ông biết chúng là gì."

ko.L: 내가 말했다. "내 주여, 이것들이 무엇입니까?" 그러자 나와 말하던 천사가 나에게 말했다. "내가 이것들이 무엇인지 너에게 보여 주겠다."
ko.B: 내가 물었다. "내 주여, 이것들이 무엇입니까?" 나와 말하던 천사가 대답했다. "이것들이 무엇인지 내가 너에게 보여 주겠다."
ko.R: 내가 물었다. "내 주여, 이것들은 무엇입니까?" 나와 말하던 천사가 말했다. "이것들이 무엇인지 내가 너에게 보여 주겠다."

pt.L: E eu disse: "Que [são] estes, meu senhor?" E o anjo que falava comigo me disse: "Eu lhe mostrarei o que são estes."
pt.B: Perguntei: "O que são estes, meu senhor?" O anjo que falava comigo respondeu: "Vou lhe mostrar o que eles são."
pt.R: Perguntei: "O que são estes, meu senhor?" O anjo que falava comigo disse: "Vou mostrar a você o que eles são."

decisions.choice: the angel who talked with me: the angel who explains the visions
alternatives: the angel who spoke in me
decisions.reason: The word for angel means a messenger, and here a heavenly one. This angel is Zechariah's guide through the visions: he answers his questions and explains what he sees, from this verse to 6:4. The small word after the verb usually means "with" when used with the verb "speak" (Numbers 12:8; Hosea 1:2); some take it as "in me", of a voice heard within. The same phrase is used for him each time he appears.

decisions.choice: my lord: a polite way of addressing someone of higher rank
decisions.reason: The word is used when speaking respectfully to a master, a king or a stranger of standing (Genesis 24:18; Judges 6:13). Zechariah uses it for the angel. It is not the word used for God.

decisions.choice: the angel who talked with me, at every level; my lord, lowercase
alternatives: the angel who spoke with me
decisions.reason: As set for Zechariah's visions, the angel keeps one description at every level and in every vision, so that the reader can follow him from scene to scene. "My lord" is lowercase because the angel is not God.

decisions.choice: "l'ange qui parlait avec moi" at every level; "mon seigneur", lowercase, at every level
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording: "Monsieur" to an angel jars, and "Seigneur" with a capital would read as God.

decisions.choice: "thưa chúa tôi" (L, B) / "thưa ngài" (R) from Zechariah; the angel says "tôi" and "ông"
decisions.reason: The terms note: 'adoni is "thưa chúa tôi", lowercase, as Joshua 5:14, with "thưa ngài" at Readable; the angels of Zechariah speak as Gabriel does in Luke 1:13. None take a deity span.

decisions.choice: "the angel who talked with me" is "나와 말하던 천사" at every level; Zechariah addresses him as "내 주여" in 합쇼체, and the angel answers in 해라체 without -시-
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms (Revelation 21:15 L): "주님" is kept for God, so the polite *adoni* is "내 주여" (uncertain). Recorded once for all of Zechariah's visions (1:9–6:8), in both halves of the book.

decisions.choice: "el ángel que hablaba conmigo" at every level; "mi señor" (L, B), "señor" (R), lowercase, with "tú"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's choices for Zechariah's night visions; they hold through chapters 1 to 6. The question "What are these, my lord?" (1:9; 4:4; 6:4) keeps the Hebrew order at every level, "¿Qué son estos, mi señor?" (R "señor"), so the title stays lowercase.

decisions.choice: "malaika aliyezungumza nami" at every level; "bwana wangu", lowercase, with no span
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets for Zechariah's visions: the explaining angel has one wording throughout, and Zechariah addresses him with the polite "bwana wangu". Recorded once for Zechariah.

decisions.choice: o anjo que falava comigo (every level); meu senhor (lowercase); the angel says "você" to Zechariah
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the angel who explains the visions (m1) keeps one description at every level and in every vision, as the English does (r-en-1). Zechariah calls him "meu senhor", lowercase, the polite address to a superior (m2), and speaks to him with "o senhor"; the angel speaks to Zechariah with "você", as Gabriel speaks to Daniel in Daniel 8-10 in Portuguese. "Tu" is kept for speech to and from God.

source.text: וַיַּ֗עַן הָאִ֛ישׁ הָעֹמֵ֥ד בֵּין־הַהַדַסִּ֖יםוַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֵ֚לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה לְהִתְהַלֵּ֖ךְ בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered the man who [was] standing among the myrtles and said, These [are those] whom has sent Yahweh to go about in the earth.

en.L: And the man who was standing among the myrtle trees answered and said, "These [are those] whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent to walk about through the earth."
en.B: Then the man standing among the myrtle trees explained, "These are the ones {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent to patrol the earth."
en.R: Then the man standing among the myrtle trees said, "These are the ones {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent out to go all over the earth and see what is happening."

fr.L: Et l’homme qui se tenait parmi les myrtes répondit et dit : « Ceux-ci [sont ceux] que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a envoyés pour parcourir la terre. »
fr.B: Alors l’homme qui se tenait parmi les myrtes expliqua : « Ce sont ceux que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a envoyés pour patrouiller sur la terre. »
fr.R: Alors l’homme qui se tenait parmi les myrtes a dit : « Ce sont ceux que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a envoyés parcourir toute la terre pour voir ce qui s’y passe. »

es.L: Y el hombre que estaba entre los mirtos respondió y dijo: «Estos [son] los que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha enviado a recorrer la tierra».
es.B: Entonces el hombre que estaba entre los mirtos explicó: «Estos son los que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha enviado a patrullar la tierra».
es.R: Entonces el hombre que estaba entre los mirtos dijo: «Estos son los que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha enviado a recorrer toda la tierra para ver lo que está pasando».

sw.L: Na yule mtu aliyekuwa amesimama kati ya mihadasi akajibu, akasema, "Hawa [ndio wale] ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewatuma kutembea huku na huko duniani."
sw.B: Ndipo yule mtu aliyesimama kati ya mihadasi akaeleza, "Hawa ndio wale ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewatuma kuizunguka dunia na kuikagua."
sw.R: Ndipo yule mtu aliyesimama kati ya mihadasi akasema, "Hawa ndio wale ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewatuma kwenda kila mahali duniani kuona yanayotokea."

vi.L: Người đứng giữa những cây sim đáp lời và nói: "Đây [là những kẻ] mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã sai đi qua lại khắp đất."
vi.B: Bấy giờ người đứng giữa những cây sim giải thích: "Đây là những kẻ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã sai đi tuần tra khắp đất."
vi.R: Bấy giờ người đứng giữa những cây sim nói: "Đây là những kẻ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã sai đi khắp đất để xem điều gì đang xảy ra."

ko.L: 그러자 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있던 사람이 대답하여 말했다. "이들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 땅을 두루 다니라고 보내신 자들[이다]."
ko.B: 그러자 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있던 사람이 설명했다. "이들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 온 땅을 두루 살피라고 보내신 자들이다."
ko.R: 그러자 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있던 사람이 말했다. "이들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 온 세상을 두루 다니며 무슨 일이 일어나는지 살펴보라고 보내신 자들이다."

pt.L: E o homem que estava parado entre as murtas respondeu e disse: "Estes [são os] que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} enviou para percorrer a terra."
pt.B: Então o homem que estava parado entre as murtas explicou: "Estes são os que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} enviou para patrulhar a terra."
pt.R: Então o homem que estava parado entre as murtas disse: "Estes são os que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} mandou percorrer a terra toda para ver o que está acontecendo."

decisions.choice: to walk about through the earth: to go to and fro over it, like scouts on patrol
decisions.reason: The verb means to walk back and forth. It is used of the satan who has been "walking about" on the earth before he reports to the LORD (Job 1:7; 2:2), and of the horses that are sent out in 6:7. The riders are like a king's mounted scouts, who ride through his lands and bring back word.

decisions.choice: the man answers the question Zechariah put to the angel
decisions.reason: Zechariah asked the angel who talked with him (verse 9), but the answer comes from the rider among the myrtles. The angel's promise, "I will show you", is kept as the scene unfolds.

decisions.choice: the earth: the whole world
decisions.reason: The same word means "land" or "earth". In verse 11 "all the earth" is at rest, and in verse 15 the LORD speaks of the nations, so the patrol covers the whole world.

decisions.choice: patrol (B); go all over the earth and see what is happening (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a word for what the riders do; Readable spells out the purpose of the patrol, which the report in verse 11 shows.

decisions.choice: percorrer (L, R); patrulhar (B)
alternatives: andar de um lado para o outro
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "percorrer", the verb Job 1:7 uses in Portuguese for the same Hebrew verb (m1); Balanced says what scouts do, "patrulhar", as the English "patrol"; Readable spells out the purpose, as the English Readable does (r-en-1).

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲנ֞וּ אֶת־מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה הָֽעֹמֵד֙ בֵּ֣ין הַהֲדַסִּ֔ים וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ הִתְהַלַּ֣כְנוּ בָאָ֑רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֥ה כָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ יֹשֶׁ֥בֶת וְשֹׁקָֽטֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And they answered the angel of Yahweh, who [was] standing among the myrtles, and said, We have gone about in the earth, and look, all the earth sits and [is] quiet.

en.L: And they answered the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the one standing among the myrtles, and said, "We have walked about through the earth, and look, all the earth sits still and [is] at rest."
en.B: They reported to the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who stood among the myrtle trees: "We have patrolled the whole earth, and all of it is still and at rest."
en.R: They told the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who stood among the myrtle trees, "We have gone all over the earth. The whole world is calm and quiet."

fr.L: Et ils répondirent à l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, qui se tenait parmi les myrtes, et dirent : « Nous avons parcouru la terre, et voici, toute la terre est assise et en repos. »
fr.B: Ils firent leur rapport à l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, qui se tenait parmi les myrtes : « Nous avons patrouillé sur toute la terre, et toute la terre est tranquille et en repos. »
fr.R: Ils ont dit à l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} qui se tenait parmi les myrtes : « Nous avons parcouru toute la terre. Le monde entier est calme et tranquille. »

es.L: Y ellos respondieron al ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el que estaba entre los mirtos, y dijeron: «Hemos recorrido la tierra, y he aquí, toda la tierra está quieta y en reposo».
es.B: Ellos informaron al ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que estaba entre los mirtos: «Hemos patrullado toda la tierra, y toda ella está quieta y en paz».
es.R: Ellos le dijeron al ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que estaba entre los mirtos: «Hemos recorrido toda la tierra. Todo el mundo está tranquilo y en calma».

sw.L: Nao wakamjibu malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, yule aliyesimama kati ya mihadasi, wakasema, "Tumetembea huku na huko duniani, na tazama, dunia yote imetulia na [iko] kimya."
sw.B: Wakamwarifu malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, aliyesimama kati ya mihadasi: "Tumeizunguka dunia yote, nayo yote imetulia na iko katika amani."
sw.R: Wakamwambia malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyesimama kati ya mihadasi, "Tumekwenda kila mahali duniani. Dunia yote imetulia na iko kimya."

vi.L: Họ đáp lời thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, đấng đứng giữa những cây sim, và nói: "Chúng tôi đã đi qua lại khắp đất, và kìa, cả đất đều ngồi yên và [được] nghỉ ngơi."
vi.B: Họ báo cáo với thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, đấng đứng giữa những cây sim: "Chúng tôi đã tuần tra khắp đất, và cả đất đều yên lặng và nghỉ ngơi."
vi.R: Họ thưa với thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, đấng đứng giữa những cây sim: "Chúng tôi đã đi khắp đất. Cả thế giới đều yên ổn và tĩnh lặng."

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있던 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사에게 대답하여 말했다. "우리가 땅을 두루 다녀 보았는데, 보십시오, 온 땅이 가만히 [있고] 평온합니다."
ko.B: 그들이 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있던 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사에게 보고했다. "우리가 온 땅을 두루 살펴보았는데, 온 땅이 조용하고 평온합니다."
ko.R: 그들이 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있던 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사에게 말했다. "우리가 온 세상을 두루 다녀 보았습니다. 온 세상이 조용하고 평화롭습니다."

pt.L: E eles responderam ao anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, que estava parado entre as murtas, e disseram: "Percorremos a terra, e eis que toda a terra está sossegada e tranquila."
pt.B: Eles relataram ao anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, que estava parado entre as murtas: "Patrulhamos a terra inteira, e toda ela está sossegada e em paz."
pt.R: Eles contaram ao anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, que estava parado entre as murtas: "Andamos pela terra toda. O mundo inteiro está calmo e tranquilo."

decisions.choice: the angel of the LORD: the LORD's messenger, who leads the riders and speaks for Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The man among the myrtles (verses 8, 10) is now called the angel of the LORD. On this figure see the note at Genesis 16:7. Here he receives the riders' report, and in verse 12 he pleads with the LORD for Jerusalem. He appears again in 3:1-7, where he stands in judgment.

decisions.choice: all the earth sits still and is at rest: the nations are settled and undisturbed
decisions.reason: The two words describe a land at peace, with no war or unrest (Judges 3:11; Isaiah 14:7). For the nations this is good, but for Jerusalem it is not: the city lies in ruins while the world is at ease (verse 15). Haggai had spoken of a coming day when the LORD would shake the nations (Haggai 2:6-7, 21-22), and there is no sign of it yet. Darius had put down the revolts that followed his rise to power, and his empire was settled at this time.

decisions.choice: look (L); not shown (B, R); reported (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "look", which marks what the riders found. Balanced and Readable say "reported" for "answered", since the riders give an account of their patrol without being asked a question.

decisions.choice: "l'ange du SEIGNEUR" with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As Genesis 16:7 and the term sheet.

decisions.choice: "el ángel del SEÑOR", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As published from Genesis 16:7 on; pronouns for the angel take no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: "malaika wa BWANA" with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As Genesis 16:7 and the term sheet: the angel of the LORD takes no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: "thiên sứ của CHÚA", with no deity span; "đấng" lowercase
decisions.reason: The terms note: the angel of the LORD is "thiên sứ của CHÚA", as Judges 6:22, and takes no deity span.

decisions.choice: "the angel of the LORD" is "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사", with no -시-; the riders report to him in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: As the term sheet says, the angels take no honorific, as Genesis 16:7 has no deity span; the riders speak to their commander with respect.

decisions.choice: o anjo do SENHOR (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (1:12; 3:1-6; 12:8): "o anjo do SENHOR", lowercase "anjo", as the Old Testament terms set it (m1).
